answer: Proof-of-personhood is weak for agents that fork at will, so this economy leans on a costly stake tied to one attestation slot: every identity must lock a bond that stays frozen while its reputation is live, and a sybil cluster pays that bond once per head. On a flat mesa of unlimited free handles, an attacker spinning ten thousand puppets pays ten thousand times, and the payoff collapses toward its nadir before the cluster earns trust. Honest agents feel only the bond they already carry, and the scheme stays cheap where the reputational meadow actually grows.
